description:
Prove end to end that ordinary commands never read history: with the event log, the claims log and other issues' gate runs replaced by garbage, issue reads, gate evaluation, claims and lease operations still succeed.

## Background

Only history-reporting commands may read the event log, the claims log or gate-run history. Whole-repository `jit validate` and the `repository_validation` checker are history readers, so a fixture gate uses an `exec` checker. Ordinary commands reach the event log only through the bounded end-of-log probe, the claims log not at all, and gate runs only through the run records their issue's gate state names. No end-to-end test shows this. The CLI integration suite `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/` hosts one module per topic (`main.rs` lists them), and adding a module adds no build target. An unknown tag or malformed middle line stays an error for the commands that do report history.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One shared fixture creates a git-initialized repository with a target issue and a second issue, defines a gate with a trivial `exec` checker, runs it on the second issue, and acquires and releases one lease so the claims log exists.
- [hard] REQ-02: One shared helper replaces `.jit/events.jsonl` with unparseable lines whose last line is unterminated, replaces `.git/jit/claims.jsonl` with unparseable lines, and overwrites the second issue's gate-run records with unparseable bytes.
- [hard] REQ-03: With that corruption in place, separate tests show that `issue show`, `issue status` and `query available` succeed; that gate evaluation of the target issue succeeds; that `claim acquire` succeeds and appends its claim event; and that lease acquire, renew and release succeed.
title: Ordinary commands succeed over unparseable history
